title: MLOps
subtitle: Tracking experiments, CI/CD for ML, and monitoring

content.text: MLOps applies DevOps principles to ML: version experiments, automate retraining, and monitor models in production.

content.code:
import mlflow

with mlflow.start_run():
    model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, max_depth=10)
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    acc = model.score(X_test, y_test)

    # Log parameters and metrics
    mlflow.log_param("n_estimators", 100)
    mlflow.log_param("max_depth", 10)
    mlflow.log_metric("accuracy", acc)

    # Log the model
    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, "model")

content.definition: Open-source platform for tracking experiments, packaging code, and deploying models.

content.text: Version your training data as well as your code. A model is only reproducible if you can recreate the exact dataset.

questions.question: What does MLflow track?
options: Parameters, metrics, and artifacts across experiment runs
questions.explanation: MLflow tracks parameters, metrics, and artifacts (models, plots) for each experiment run, enabling comparison.

faq.a: A centralised repository for computed features, ensuring consistency between training and serving. Tools include Feast and Hopsworks.
